correctness.rationale: This passes the actual corrected RESULT.md in /workspace/repairs/2, not the frozen Finding. Its unqualified interior-positive sentence fails: at N=2, a=1, b=1/2, U=1, m=1/4, δ=1/100, t=1/2, physical reservoirs give R=3/25<F_3=18/7 and exact currents (−143,−43,−143)/2800. The proof in the frozen file had used the extra assumption R>2. The replacement keeps the valid all-link cutoff, restricts the interior-positive guarantee under F_L>R to R≥2, and documents the counterexample. In the exact one-point Dirichlet problem, T is affine and M is proportional to sinh(λ(j−L/2)); for N=1 both reservoir generators act on the sole site. Differences of M are a positive constant times cosh(λ(j+1/2−L/2)), strictly largest at the two endpoints except when there are only those endpoints. The minimum current is therefore (a−b)m(R−F_L)/(2L); the telescoping sum is (a−b)m(R−2)/2. If both endpoints are strictly negative and that sum is nonnegative, a positive interior link must exist, including R=2 when L>2. The log derivative of F_L is 1/L−c cosh(c)/(sinh(Lc)cosh((L−1)c))>0 for c=λ/2 and L≥2; F_2=2 and F_L~L(1−z). An independent rational propagation of the recurrence checked the two published example vectors and the counterexample. The frozen script and output were inspected, not executed; their R=18/5 example does not certify the original unqualified sentence. The repair also corrects the attribution about the hydrodynamic limit and keeps the constitutive-current restriction.

value.rationale: The corrected result gives a necessary and sufficient size criterion for when the opposing gradients can sustain uphill constitutive A-current even at the reservoirs, and distinguishes boundary reversal from loss of all positive currents. This is a meaningful finite-chain cutoff independent of the particular rational illustration; neither a finite sample nor a continuum bound answers that length question.
